think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 27-year-old immigrant presenting with chronic bilateral antibiotic-refractory otitis media, bilateral profound sensorineural/conductive deafness, progressive cranial neuropathies (CN VI and VII), and an invasive mass in the external auditory canals and nasopharynx with petroclival erosion and temporal pachymeningitis. The presentation heavily mimics aggressive skull base carcinoma, lymphoma, necrotizing bacterial skull base osteomyelitis, or granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA).
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission clinical and imaging evaluation including ENT examination, audiometry, baseline blood tests, chest radiography, and cranial MRI, prior to mucosal/bone biopsies, auramine staining, and interferon-gamma release assay (Quantiferon TB Gold).
3. Differential Distinctions: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma or skull base malignant neoplasia causes petroclival bone destruction, parapharyngeal space extension, and multiple cranial nerve palsies, but was ruled out by biopsy showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with giant cells; necrotizing/malignant external otitis (Pseudomonas aeruginosa) causes destructive temporal bone osteomyelitis but typically occurs in elderly diabetics and responds to antipseudomonal agents; granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) causes destructive otologic/sinonasal inflammation and pachymeningitis, but was ruled out by auramine demonstration of acid-fast bacilli and positive mycobacterial culture.
case_prompt:
A 27-year-old male immigrant from Somalia presents with an 8-month history of persistent bilateral otitis media, progressive hearing loss, and tinnitus that have failed multiple courses of oral antibiotics. Over the past two weeks, he has developed malaise, fever, anorexia, weight loss, dizziness, and an unsteady gait, followed one week later by diplopia and a right-sided facial droop. His family history is notable for a sibling treated for a chronic pulmonary infection upon immigration screening seven years earlier, at which time the patient's own chest radiograph had shown changes interpreted as past healed infection.

On physical examination, the patient is malnourished and exhibits profound bilateral deafness. Neurological examination reveals a right-sided peripheral facial nerve palsy (cranial nerve VII) and a left-sided abducens nerve palsy (cranial nerve VI). Otoscopy reveals extensive polypous inflammatory tissue obstructing both external auditory canals. Flexible nasopharyngeal endoscopy demonstrates a similar purulent inflammatory mass in the left middle nasal passage extending toward the Eustachian tube orifice.

Baseline laboratory investigations show a hemoglobin of 7.2 mmol/L (after intravenous hydration), an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 56 mm/hr, and mild transaminase elevations. HIV serology is negative. Tone audiometry demonstrates severe symmetric mixed hearing loss of 80 to 120 dB across all frequencies. A plain chest radiograph shows stable apical fibrosis in the left lower lobe, unchanged from imaging taken seven years prior. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the head and skull base reveals an aggressive inflammatory process involving both mastoid and petrous temporal bones, an abscess on the left extending into the parapharyngeal space and displacing the nasopharyngeal contour, extensive bilateral temporal pachymeningitis, and bilateral inner ear involvement.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the invasive nasopharyngeal and skull base mass causing petrous bone erosion, parapharyngeal extension, and multiple cranial neuropathies (CN VI, VII, VIII), but excluded by histology demonstrating necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and absence of malignant cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Histology of biopsies from the external ear canals as well as from the mass extending from the nasopharynx and skull base to the nose showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with giant cells.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Refractory Bacterial Otitis Media / Malignant External Otitis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to severe bilateral otorrhea and extensive temporal bone osteomyelitis, but the patient failed multiple antibacterial regimens and histological staining demonstrated acid-fast bacilli rather than typical pyogenic bacterial pathogens.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: persistent bilateral otitis media, progressive hearing loss, and tinnitus since eight months, which had been unresponsive to several courses of antibiotics.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Auramine fluorescent staining identified an acid-fast rod in the nasopharyngeal biopsy specimen, corroborated by a strongly positive Quantiferon TB Gold assay (>10 IU/mL) and definitive recovery of susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis on culture.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Auramine staining was positive with one acid-fast rod in the nasopharyngeal biopsy, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining and PCR of all biopsies were negative. The Quantiferon TB Gold in-tube assay (Cellestis, Carnegie, Australia), performed three days after starting prednisone, was positive (>10 IU/mL interferon-gamma, cut-off value 0.35 IU/mL).

editor_comments: Distilled strictly to admission triage, audiometry, and skull base MRI before biopsy histopathology, auramine staining, and Quantiferon testing. Zero spoilers or pathogen names in case_prompt. Direct verbatim quotes provided for all candidates and the diagnostic pivot.
